hits.tldr: Use @source not inline() to prevent specific classes from being generated in Tailwind CSS.
Tailwind CSS scans source as plain text, so you must use complete class names and map dynamic values to predefined class lists.
Tailwind scans source files as plain text for tokens matching expected class name characters, then generates CSS only for recognized utilities.
Use `--value([{type}])` syntax to declare which data types arbitrary utility values support.
Use inline styles in Tailwind for dynamic values from APIs/databases and complex arbitrary values.

content.text:
Your fix is the documented correct approach, not a workaround. Tailwind scans source files as **plain text** for complete class name tokens (`src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx`, "How classes are detected"). Since `{{ Vite::image('hero.jpg') }}` is a runtime-rendered Blade expression, Tailwind never sees a literal `bg-[url('hero.jpg')]` string at build time — it can't generate the CSS for it.

The docs explicitly recommend inline `style` for values coming from a dynamic source like this (`src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "When to use inline styles"): use `style="background-image: url('...')"` and keep `bg-cover bg-no-repeat bg-blend-multiply` as regular utility classes.
